dct_description_sm: We wish to recognize and thank the literally thousands of Costa Rican and international people, experiences, and institutions that have contributed and continue their thinking and support for the content of this work. We are especially grateful for the staff and institutions that have created and maintained ACG since the beginning of its existence in 1966 and full germination in 1985. Without that, these ideas and reality would not exist, nor would there be the opportunity to notice what is happening to its biodiversity. This study was made possible because of awards from Canada’s New Frontiers in Research Fund (NFRFT-2020-00073) and CFI’s Major Science Infrastructure program (MSI 42450). They sustained the analytical capacity and informatics platforms at the Centre for Biodiversity Genomics at Guelph, Canada, needed to advance the overall BIOSCAN research program and its key initiatives such as BioAlfa and BOLD, with special thanks to the Walder Foundation of Chicago and the government of Costa Rica. We thank the ACG parataxonomists for sharing biological data and providing specimens that enabled the descriptions. All yy-SRNP-nnnnn and DHJPARnnnnn vouchered specimens were collected,  exported, and DNA barcoded under Costa Rican government permits issued to BioAlfa (Janzen & Hallwachs, 2019a) (R-048-2016-OT-CONAGEBIO, R-019-2019-CONAGEBIO, R-053-2019-OT-CONAGEBIO, R-013-2020-OT-CONAGEBIO, R-021-2020-OT-CONAGEBIO, R-057-2021-OT-CONAGEBIO, R-054-2021- OT-CONAGEBIO, R-012-2022-OT-CONAGEBIO, R-023-2022-OT-CONAGEBIO, R-054-2022-OT-CONAGEBIO & R-006-2023-OT-CONAGEBIO; National Published Decree #41767), JICASAPI #0328497 (2014) and DHJ and WH (ACGPI-036-2013; R-SINAC-ACG-PI-061-2021; Resolution Nº001-2004 SINAC; PI-028-2021). Finally, we thank the rangers of the National System of Conservation Areas (SINAC) for collecting specimens from Malaise traps in protected areas.

Underlying raw data for all insect samples DNA barcoded following collection via 28 Malaise traps across Costa Rica (3, 777, 632 DNA barcodes that represented 152, 891 BINs (Barcode Index Numbers) from 28 localities).
dct_title_s: Replication data for: Massive DNA barcoding reveals highly distinct insect distribution patterns across Costa Rican ecosystems
